content: GLUCOPHAGE (Metformin Hydrochloride Tablets) The standard initial dose of GLUCOPHAGE is 500 mg taken twice daily or 850 mg taken once daily, both administered with meals. If dose adjustments are needed, they should be made in increments of 500 mg weekly or 850 mg every two weeks, with a maximum total daily dose of 2000 mg, divided into multiple doses. Patients may also transition from 500 mg twice daily to 850 mg twice daily after two weeks. For patients requiring additional glycemic control, the maximum allowable daily dose is 2550 mg. Doses exceeding 2000 mg per day may be better tolerated when administered three times daily with meals. GLUCOPHAGE XR (Metformin Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets) The typical starting dose of GLUCOPHAGE XR is 500 mg taken once daily with the evening meal. Dose increases should occur in 500 mg increments weekly, up to a maximum of 2000 mg taken once daily with the evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved with 2000 mg once daily, a trial of 1000 mg taken twice daily may be considered. For patients requiring higher doses of metformin, the standard GLUCOPHAGE formulation should be used, with a maximum daily dose of 2550 mg divided into multiple doses. Switching from GLUCOPHAGE to GLUCOPHAGE XR Clinical trials have demonstrated that patients currently on GLUCOPHAGE can be safely transitioned to GLUCOPHAGE XR at the same total daily dose, up to a maximum of 2000 mg once daily. After switching, glycemic control should be closely monitored, and dose adjustments should be made as necessary. Transitioning from Other Antidiabetic Therapies When transitioning patients from other oral hypoglycemic agents (excluding chlorpropamide) to GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR, no specific transition period is typically required. However, when switching from chlorpropamide, caution is advised during the first two weeks due to the prolonged retention of chlorpropamide in the body, which may result in overlapping drug effects and an increased risk of hypoglycemia. Combined Therapy with GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR and Oral Sulfonylureas If patients fail to achieve adequate glycemic control after four weeks of maximum-dose monotherapy with GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR, an oral sulfonylurea may be added gradually while maintaining the maximum dose of GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR. This approach may be considered even in cases of prior primary or secondary failure with sulfonylureas. Clinical and pharmacokinetic data on drug interactions are currently available only for the combination of metformin and glyburide (glibenclamide). If glycemic control remains unsatisfactory after one to three months of combined therapy at maximum doses, alternative treatments, such as insulin therapy with or without GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR, should be considered. Combined Therapy with GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR and Insulin When initiating GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR in patients already on insulin therapy, the current insulin dose should be maintained. GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR should be started at 500 mg once daily. If glycemic control is inadequate, the dose of GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR can be increased by 500 mg weekly until the desired glycemic control is achieved. The maximum recommended daily dose is 2500 mg for GLUCOPHAGE and 2000 mg for GLUCOPHAGE XR. When fasting plasma glucose levels drop below 120 mg/dL, the insulin dose should be reduced by 10% to 25%. Further adjustments should be individualized based on the patient’s glucose-lowering response. Special Considerations for Specific Patient Populations GLUCOPHAGE and GLUCOPHAGE XR are not recommended for use during pregnancy or in pediatric patients. In elderly patients, initial and maintenance doses should be conservative due to the potential for reduced renal function. Dose adjustments should be based on a thorough evaluation of renal function. Elderly, debilitated, or malnourished patients should generally not be titrated to the maximum dose of GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR. Renal function should be closely monitored in all patients, particularly the elderly, to minimize the risk of lactic acidosis.
